entries.title: Admission, evidence or recovery failure in the brownfield adoption service

entries.checks: The rule verifies the conformance evidence an adapter produces for its declared target; the adapter host refuses to trust an adapter whose checks or contracts do not hold.

examples.after:
# Fix the mismatch the conformance check reports (for example the
# pinned contract version), then re-install or re-run the adapter:
lekalo adapter update --target demo
lekalo adapter test --target demo

fixOptions.description: Re-run the adapter's documented install/update flow so checks and evidence are regenerated against the pinned contract versions; never edit conformance evidence by hand.
Reproduce the failing check with the adapter's own diagnostics before changing any project source.

entries.rationale: It matters because a non-conforming adapter can silently corrupt generated artifacts, misreport target behavior, or break the portability guarantees every downstream consumer relies on.
rootCauses: the installed adapter version does not match the contract version the project pins
the adapter's generated artifacts or inventory were edited by hand after generation
the target toolchain or runtime changed underneath the adapter
conformance evidence was produced against a different project revision

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Waivable only for explicitly trusted local development adapters; the underlying conformance gap remains and must be re-checked after any adapter or contract update.

targetNotes.note: Target-specific: the exact check names and artifact homes are defined by the target's adapter SDK contract; consult the adapter's manifest for its declared conformance surface.

examples.after:

entries.checks: The rule flags a construct whose meaning cannot be proven from the admitted input and records every candidate interpretation as data instead of guessing one.

examples.after:
# keep exactly one proven interpretation
observed: explicit-call

an external producer emitted overlapping claims without a priority

entries.checks: The rule enforces the declared architecture profile: dependency directions, allowed relations and layer boundaries between modules.

examples.after:
# after moving the dependency (or consciously updating the profile):
lekalo architecture-profile resolve
lekalo architecture-profile diff --base base.json
examples.before:
# planner depends on transport, forbidden by the profile
lekalo architecture-profile diff --base base.json

fixOptions.description: Either move the offending dependency back inside the allowed boundary or update the profile intentionally, then re-lock and re-run the comparison.

entries.rationale: It matters because profiles are the machine-checked form of the agreed architecture; violations left unflagged let the module graph drift until refactors become unbounded.
rootCauses: a new dependency crosses a boundary the profile forbids
a module was renamed or moved without updating the profile
the profile was edited without re-deriving its lock from the graph

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Profile exceptions belong in the reviewed profile document itself, not in per-run waivers; a diagnostic suppressed elsewhere still fails the profile gate.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: profiles constrain the semantic module graph, not generated code.

examples.after:

a subject or action references evidence that is missing or revoked
two rules overlap without an explicit precedence declaration

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: authorization invariants are security boundaries; fix the model instead.

entries.checks: The rule checks the binding pipeline that connects native source symbols to semantic IDs: proposal shape, confirmation state and custody.

examples.after:
lekalo bindings propose --target node-typescript
lekalo bindings confirm --binding <id>

fixOptions.description: Re-run the scan to regenerate proposals, then confirm the corrected binding explicitly; delete stale custody rather than editing it.

entries.rationale: It matters because bindings are the trust anchor between generated and native code; an unconfirmed or stale binding silently redirects semantic guarantees to the wrong code.
rootCauses: a proposal was edited instead of being re-derived by a fresh scan
the native file changed after the binding was confirmed
two proposals claim the same semantic ID or native symbol

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: binding custody is what makes native evidence referable; refresh instead.

targetNotes.note: Binding homes and custody are target-specific and defined by each adapter's SDK; the semantic IDs they anchor are not.

entries.checks: The rule admits semantic change requests and owns their bounded plans, transactions, receipts and idempotent replay.

examples.after:
lekalo change preview --request r.json
lekalo change apply --request r.json --expect-plan <fresh-plan-id>

fixOptions.description: Re-preview the change against current inputs and apply with the fresh exact plan ID; recover interrupted transactions with lekalo change recover --transaction <id> before new writes.

entries.rationale: It matters because every durable source mutation flows through this service; a custody or admission gap here would let unreviewed writes land or destroy rollback ability.
rootCauses: the change request references symbols absent from the current inputs
the exact preview plan ID was not supplied at apply time, or inputs drifted
a transaction journal from an interrupted run was not recovered

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: admission and custody are the mutation safety envelope.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: change owns Model/source custody; target regeneration is a separate explicit request.

entries.checks: The rule checks the CI report projections (JSON, SARIF, JUnit, annotations) and their custody when a run writes them.

examples.after: lekalo validate --report-file reports/validate.sarif --report-format sarif

fixOptions.description: Fix the report path/permissions or drop the unsupported format; the underlying run verdict is separate and unchanged either way.

entries.rationale: It matters because CI consumers act on these reports; a mis-projected report can turn a failed gate green in the hosting system even though the run failed.
rootCauses: the report file could not be written (permissions, confined runner)
the requested format is not available for this run kind
report provenance pins do not match the executed inputs

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: report integrity failures must be visible in CI.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: projections consume the result envelope only.

entries.checks: The rule rejects malformed command-line syntax before any domain work starts.

examples.after: lekalo fix --recipe r.json --allow-unsafe

fixOptions.description: Fix the invocation per lekalo <command> --help; usage errors exit 2 and are owned by the CLI parser, not by DomainResult statuses.

entries.rationale: It matters because usage refusals stay typed: scripts and agents get the stable cli.usage diagnostic instead of parser noise on stdout.
rootCauses: a required argument is missing or two flags conflict
an argument value is outside its bounded range or closed vocabulary

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: there is nothing to waive; correct the command line.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral.

entries.checks: The rule enforces the declared data classifications and the classified data-flow policy over the semantic graph.

examples.after:
# add the classification to the field or declare the transition,
# then:
lekalo dataflow --project .
examples.before: lekalo dataflow --project .   # unclassified field on a path

fixOptions.description: Classify the offending data explicitly or declare (and review) the flow transition; then re-run the flow report.

entries.rationale: It matters because classification rules keep sensitive data out of flows that were never reviewed; bypassing them silently breaks the project's privacy guarantees.
rootCauses: a field or effect lacks the classification its consumers assume
a flow crosses a classification boundary without a declared, reviewed transition
the policy was edited without re-deriving dependent evidence

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Classification exceptions need the classification-policy attachment, not ad-hoc waivers.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: classifications ride the Model; adapters project them per target policy.

entries.checks: The rule validates context capsules and their assembly: bounded projections of semantic facts for AI consumption.

examples.after: lekalo context --symbols <bounded selection>

fixOptions.description: Narrow the capsule selection or raise the policy consciously; re-assemble after the inputs or evidence change.

entries.rationale: It matters because capsules are the AI-facing read model; overflow or unproven content here directly degrades every downstream agent answer.
rootCauses: a capsule requested more symbols or bytes than the policy allows
assembly included evidence that is not admitted for the requesting consumer

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: bounds are the product, not an obstacle.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: capsules are derived only from admitted semantic facts.

entries.checks: The rule reports a data flow that crosses a declared classification boundary without an admitted transition.

examples.after:
# reclassify or declare the transition, then:
lekalo dataflow --project .
examples.before: lekalo dataflow --project .   # public query reads confidential

fixOptions.description: Reclassify the field consciously or insert a declared, reviewed transition; re-run the data-flow report afterwards.

entries.rationale: It matters because these flows are exactly the paths sensitive data leaks through; each refusal is a reviewed privacy boundary holding.
rootCauses: a field's classification changed while its flows stayed unchanged
an effect or query reads classified data the flow report never admitted

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Policy transitions live in the classification policy, not per-run waivers.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: flows are Model-level; target storage policies consume them.

entries.checks: The rule compares two typed projections and classifies every change as breaking, non-breaking or policy-only.

entries.checks: The rule guards the explanation service itself: the embedded catalog's integrity, its registry pin, and the readability of caller-supplied reports.

examples.after: lekalo explain LEK-HIDDEN-009   # registered code, explained
examples.before: lekalo explain LEK-TYPE-014   # illustrative, unregistered code

fixOptions.description: For unknown codes, check the spelling against the catalog version in the result; for report refusals, supply a report with a readable diagnostics array. Catalog-integrity failures are developer faults: rebuild from a clean checkout.

entries.rationale: It matters because explanations are the stable contract humans and AI read instead of per-run text; a broken catalog or an unreadable report must refuse visibly rather than serve an unproven explanation.
rootCauses: the requested code or rule id is not in this catalog (distinct unexplained outcome)
the embedded catalog drifted from the registry union it pins
the --diagnostic-file input is malformed, over-limit, or carries no diagnostics

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: service-integrity refusals are typed outcomes, not policy.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: explanations resolve offline from the embedded catalog.

examples.before: # declaration pinned to old artifact digest

entries.checks: The rule records indirection the admitted inputs cannot resolve to a concrete target, keeping the gap visible.

examples.after: # declare the handler set and select with a closed vocabulary

fixOptions.description: Replace runtime string selection with declared references, or record the key set explicitly so the indirection becomes analyzable.

entries.rationale: It matters because indirection through config or strings is invisible to static guarantee systems unless surfaced; this rule makes the ambiguity explicit.
rootCauses: behavior is selected through configuration values unknown at analysis time
a registry/lookup pattern maps keys to handlers without declared edges

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: informational; the uncertainty stays recorded.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral.

entries.title: Unproven indirection retained

entries.checks: The rule guards project bootstrap: creation, adoption and the first admitted structure of a project.

examples.after: # classify or move the strays, then re-run adoption

fixOptions.description: Start from an empty directory, or reconcile the existing structure with the documented adoption flow; never force-create over an owned project.

entries.rationale: It matters because a project created or adopted with an unproven structure carries that debt into every later gate; bootstrap refusals keep the foundation honest.
rootCauses: the target directory already contains an incompatible project
adoption inputs reference files outside the admitted boundary
the generated skeleton conflicts with the chosen mode

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: the first structure is the root of custody.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: bootstrap writes only the canonical project homes.

entries.checks: The rule resolves a semantic symbol for inspection and reports selections that cannot be resolved unambiguously.

examples.after: lekalo inspect planner.save_task

fixOptions.description: Use the full semantic id, or resolve the ambiguity with search first; consult rename history for moved symbols.

entries.rationale: It matters because inspect output feeds agents and humans; a wrong-symbol answer is worse than a typed refusal, so ambiguity refuses.
rootCauses: the short name matches multiple symbols in the project
the symbol was removed or renamed (check rename history)

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: selection refusals are precise, not policy.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: inspection reads the compiled projection.

entries.checks: The rule checks declared state invariants and their transitions for reachability and preservation.

examples.after: # guard the transition on title non-empty
examples.before: # transition sets done=true with empty title

fixOptions.description: Constrain the transition or refine the invariant so every reachable state satisfies it; re-run the transition check afterwards.

entries.rationale: It matters because broken invariants are the deep bugs: data states no review anticipated; checking transitions is the only systematic coverage.
rootCauses: a transition can enter a state the invariant forbids
an invariant references fields a transition legitimately mutates

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: reachable violations block release gates.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: invariants live in the Model.

entries.checks: The rule compiles the Model into the typed IR and refuses documents that cannot produce a proven intermediate representation.

examples.after: # define or re-point the reference, then recompile

fixOptions.description: Correct the Model against the current grammar (see the loader/semantic rules the envelope also carries) and recompile.

entries.rationale: It matters because the IR is the read model every projection builds on; compiling a questionable Model would propagate doubt into all downstream outputs.
rootCauses: a document uses a construct outside the admitted grammar generation
references between definitions do not resolve
version pins between Model and IR contracts are incompatible

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: without IR there is nothing downstream to trust.

targetNotes.note: Adapters consume the versioned IR; its version is pinned per adapter contract.

entries.checks: The rule admits project files into the typed Model: canonical homes, encoding, bounded sizes and the closed YAML/JSON grammar.

examples.after: # rewrite without anchors/aliases in the closed subset

fixOptions.description: Move the file to its canonical home and correct the syntax/fields the envelope names; run lekalo format afterwards to keep documents canonical.

entries.rationale: It matters because loading is the trust boundary between arbitrary bytes and the semantic system; every later guarantee assumes what the loader admitted.
rootCauses: a file sits outside its canonical home or is unreadable/over-limit
syntax outside the closed YAML/JSON subset (anchors, flow style, duplicate keys)
schema fields are unknown, misspelled, or use a foreign generation

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: grammar refusals define the language.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: the loader owns Model documents, never target source.

entries.checks: The rule guards the read-only MCP server's project scope, protocol pins, bounded requests, stable snapshots and safe typed responses.

examples.after:
lekalo mcp describe --json
# correct the trusted launcher configuration or refresh the request
# within its admitted project scope, then retry the read-only tool
examples.before: # a tool request names an unregistered project or stale revision

fixOptions.description: Check the diagnostic's rule and the documented MCP tool contract; use only a project, group and input admitted by the trusted launcher configuration.

For stale snapshots or transient deadlines, request fresh evidence within the admitted bounds. Correct backend or disclosure failures before retrying; do not bypass confinement, redact required fields or silently downgrade a protocol pin.

entries.rationale: It matters because an agent must receive a complete, current result within the explicitly admitted project scope; a refusal must not widen access, disclose sensitive data or silently change the protocol.
rootCauses: the request or trusted server configuration violates the selected tool's scope, schema, protocol pin or resource limits
an authorized input changed, the request was cancelled or its deadline expired before a complete response existed
a required safe backend is unavailable or its output cannot satisfy the selected contract and disclosure policy

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: scope, disclosure, resource and protocol boundaries remain enforced.

targetNotes.note: Host-specific safe-read and confinement capabilities remain mandatory. The MCP surface never grants source writes or generation authority.

entries.checks: The rule guards the versioned module public contract: exported surface, dependency boundaries, locks and compatibility diffs.

examples.after: # decide: restore the surface or accept + re-lock, then re-diff

fixOptions.description: Restore the exported surface, or make the API change intentionally: refresh the module lock and re-run the diff to classify the delta.

entries.rationale: It matters because the public API is what sibling modules and external consumers build against; unflagged drift breaks them at their compile or runtime, not at review time.
rootCauses: a change removed or reshaped an exported member without a versioned lock update
a new dependency crosses the module boundary the contract declares
the lock was not refreshed after a legitimate API change

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: boundary drift must be a reviewed decision, never noise.

targetNotes.note: Per-adapter: generated public surfaces are projected per target; the contract is Model-level.

entries.title: NFR gate failure

entries.checks: The rule admits native gate plans and runs: bounded declarations, custody preconditions and typed refusals instead of guesses.

examples.after: # regenerate custody + plan, then run

fixOptions.description: Regenerate the plan from current custody; run only within the admitted scope, and record the typed refusal honestly when confinement is unavailable.

entries.rationale: It matters because native gates execute real target code; admitting an unproven plan would run unreviewed code with project trust.
rootCauses: a plan references custody or fixtures that are missing or stale
the requested execution exceeds the admitted plan scope
the platform cannot provide the required confinement

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: native execution outside admitted custody is the harm this family prevents.

targetNotes.note: Confinement backends and availability are platform-specific (e.g. bubblewrap on Linux); refusals are data on every OS.

examples.after: # regenerate custody + plan, then run

fixOptions.description: Regenerate the plan from current custody; run only within the admitted scope, and record the typed refusal honestly when confinement is unavailable.

entries.rationale: It matters because native gates execute real target code; admitting an unproven plan would run unreviewed code with project trust.
rootCauses: a plan references custody or fixtures that are missing or stale
the requested execution exceeds the admitted plan scope
the platform cannot provide the required confinement

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: native execution outside admitted custody is the harm this family prevents.

targetNotes.note: Confinement backends and availability are platform-specific (e.g. bubblewrap on Linux); refusals are data on every OS.

entries.checks: The rule projects the Model into the published OpenAPI surface and validates it against the OpenAPI schema.

examples.after: # regenerate from the Model, then validate

fixOptions.description: Align the Model declarations with what the projection admits, and regenerate the document through the owned flow.

entries.rationale: It matters because the OpenAPI document is a public contract for external HTTP consumers; drift here breaks clients that were promised the schema.
rootCauses: a declared operation cannot be projected (unsupported shape)
the projection drifted from the validated OpenAPI version

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: public API documents must match the Model.

targetNotes.note: Transport-specific details ride the transport contract; the projection grammar is shared.

entries.checks: The rule guards observed mode: native evidence scans, index records, freshness and candidate completeness.

examples.after: lekalo scan --project .   # fresh, then re-observe
examples.before: lekalo scan --project .   # native files changed since

fixOptions.description: Re-run the scan to refresh the index; treat unobservable domains as unknown, never as covered.

entries.rationale: It matters because observed mode is how native reality enters the semantic world; stale or partial evidence here quietly misrepresents the target.
rootCauses: the index was built from a scan older than the current native files
a scan claims coverage the backend could not actually observe
records were edited outside the scan service

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: freshness is recorded as data.

targetNotes.note: Scanner backends are per-target; freshness rules and index grammar are shared.

entries.checks: The rule admits the PHP operations-generation input and validates the resulting operations map.

examples.after: # regenerate via the generator, then re-run the gate

fixOptions.description: Regenerate the map from the admitted input through the generator; fix the input when the Model and it disagree.

entries.rationale: It matters because operations maps drive PHP code generation; a wrong map generates code that silently diverges from the Model.
rootCauses: the operations input references operations the Model does not declare
the map was edited outside the generator

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: generated code must trace to admitted input.

targetNotes.note: PHP-specific: the map feeds the PHP/Laravel adapter's operation surface.

entries.title: PHP operations map failure

entries.checks: The rule admits portability recipes, evidence and receipts that prove a Model ported to a target faithfully.

examples.after: # re-run the port flow, then re-admit fresh evidence

fixOptions.description: Re-run the port against the current revision to regenerate evidence and receipts; never re-badge old evidence with new digests.

entries.rationale: It matters because portability is the product's core promise; unproven port claims would ship adapters that diverge from the semantic truth.
rootCauses: evidence is pinned to an older Model or adapter revision
a receipt references execution that cannot be reproduced
the recipe's declared family does not match its evidence

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: port claims without evidence are the failure mode.

targetNotes.note: Per-target: evidence binds target identity and adapter SDK versions.

entries.checks: The rule validates the query model: declared reads, returns and their consistency with the entity model.

examples.after: # add the field to the entity or drop it from returns
examples.before: # query returns user.email; entity lacks email

fixOptions.description: Align the query's reads and returns with the entity model, or extend the entity consciously.

entries.rationale: It matters because queries are the read-side contract; inconsistent declarations would return data the write side never admitted.
rootCauses: a query returns fields no entity or aggregate declares
declared reads do not cover the fields the returns project

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: read/write divergence is a correctness bug.

targetNotes.note: Per-target: query translation is adapter work; the model-level contract is the authority.

entries.checks: The rule validates the published client SDK surface: envelope shape, capability advertisement and version compatibility.

examples.after:
node scripts/generate-adapter-sdk.mjs --write
node scripts/test-adapter-sdk-contracts.mjs
examples.before: node scripts/generate-adapter-sdk.mjs --write   # then edit by hand

fixOptions.description: Regenerate the SDK with the pinned generator and update consumers to the advertised capabilities; never widen the wire by hand.

entries.rationale: It matters because external consumers build on the SDK wire; drift here breaks integrations that were promised stability.
rootCauses: the SDK was generated against different contract versions than the binary serves
an envelope field was consumed that the closed schema does not carry

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: SDK compatibility is a published contract.

targetNotes.note: Per-SDK: each adapter SDK pins its own contract versions; the wire shapes stay shared.

entries.checks: The rule plans and validates storage migrations and projections from the Model to target storage.

examples.after: # restore history or re-plan as a fresh baseline, then apply
examples.before: lekalo storage laravel-plan --project .   # missing rename history

fixOptions.description: Re-plan the migration from the current Model with complete rename history; apply only through the transactional migration writer with reviewed evidence.

entries.rationale: It matters because storage mistakes lose data; migration planning refuses rather than guessing when evidence or mappings are incomplete.
rootCauses: a migration step references entities the current Model lacks
projection mappings disagree with declared fields or types
transaction or rename history is missing for an incremental step

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: data-loss risks need migration evidence, never flags.

targetNotes.note: Per-storage-engine: engine profiles define real capabilities; Model-level planning stays engine-neutral.

entries.checks: The rule admits search queries, owns the disposable local index and its coverage claims, and returns bounded selection cards.

examples.after:
lekalo search-index rebuild
lekalo search "task"

fixOptions.description: Rebuild the index when stale; correct the query grammar; treat missing coverage as explicit unknown and consult the flagged domains.

entries.rationale: It matters because search is how agents discover the project; unproven or stale results would anchor every later decision on wrong facts.
rootCauses: the index is stale relative to current sources
the query is malformed or outside the admitted grammar
coverage for a domain is missing and cannot be claimed

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: retrieval gaps are recorded, not waivable.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: search reads semantic data and admitted evidence only; no repository text scan.

entries.checks: The rule checks declared transactions for concurrency hazards: overlapping writes, lost updates and isolation assumptions.

examples.after: # declare the ordering or split the write sets, then re-run
examples.before: # tx A writes orders, tx B writes orders without ordering

fixOptions.description: Narrow the transaction's write set, declare the ordering, or align the isolation assumptions with the storage profile; then re-run the check.

rootCauses: two commands write overlapping resources without an ordering declaration
a transaction assumes an isolation level the storage profile does not provide

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: unresolved concurrency hazards block release gates.

targetNotes.note: Consult the storage engine profile for the target's actual isolation guarantees; the Model-level check is target-neutral.

entries.checks: The rule validates target profiles: declared target identity, capability claims and their evidence.

examples.after: # correct capability claims, re-admit
examples.before: # profile claims mysql window functions on sqlite

fixOptions.description: Re-derive the profile from the target's actual SDK capabilities and re-admit it with fresh evidence.

entries.rationale: It matters because profiles are how targets promise what they can do; unproven capability claims produce generated code the target cannot run.
rootCauses: a profile declares capabilities the target SDK does not provide
the profile was edited without re-admitting its evidence

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: capability claims must be true.

entries.checks: The rule admits the neutral trace manifest and validates its relations, revisions and digest pins.

examples.after: # re-export, then validate
examples.before: lekalo trace validate --manifest t.json   # stale pin

fixOptions.description: Re-export the trace from its producer against the current revision; fix relation references instead of loosening pins.

entries.rationale: It matters because traces are neutral evidence linking requirements to behavior; broken pins would validate today's claims with yesterday's artifacts.
rootCauses: the manifest references relations or symbols absent from the current revision
digest pins no longer match the cited attachments

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: staleness is recorded as data.

entries.checks: The rule validates the HTTP transport contract: declared routes, payload shapes and transport-level guarantees.

examples.after: # declare the operation in the Model and regenerate

fixOptions.description: Declare the route and payload in the Model, or remove the undeclared surface; regenerate transports from declarations.

payload shapes disagree between declaration and implementation

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: reachable undeclared surface is a security boundary.

targetNotes.note: Per-target transports differ; the declared contract is the shared authority.

scope or module selections reference unknown modules

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: run admission is precise, not policy.

entries.checks: The rule owns version transitions: compatibility classification, migration planning and the sealed migration catalog.

examples.after:
lekalo migrate --plan --from <current> --to <target>
lekalo migrate --apply --transaction <id>

fixOptions.description: Plan migrations through the owning service from the current state; never hand-write migration steps or re-classify a delta to dodge the gate.

entries.rationale: It matters because version transitions are where data is lost or contracts break; refusing unproven transitions is the whole point of the service.
rootCauses: a migration step is unknown to the sealed catalog
the transition's compatibility class disagrees with the actual delta
apply was requested without the transaction's exact evidence

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: transitions need reviewed evidence, not flags.

targetNotes.note: Per-target storage migrations add engine steps; classification semantics are shared.

fixOptions.description: Plan migrations through the owning service from the current state; never hand-write migration steps or re-classify a delta to dodge the gate.

entries.rationale: It matters because version transitions are where data is lost or contracts break; refusing unproven transitions is the whole point of the service.
rootCauses: a migration step is unknown to the sealed catalog
the transition's compatibility class disagrees with the actual delta
apply was requested without the transaction's exact evidence

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: transitions need reviewed evidence, not flags.

targetNotes.note: Per-target storage migrations add engine steps; classification semantics are shared.

entries.checks: The rule admits extended-effect declarations that go beyond the core effect grammar and enforces their evidence obligations.

examples.after: # re-attach the extension to a live effect or delete it
examples.before: # extension pinned to a removed effect

fixOptions.description: Re-admit the declaration with current evidence, or remove the extension that lost its underlying effect.

entries.rationale: It matters because extended effects extend what the graph claims about the system; unproven claims would propagate into impact, coverage and review surfaces.
rootCauses: a declaration exceeds its permitted shape or evidence binding
the underlying effect was removed while the extension remained

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: unproven effect claims are not admissible.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: extensions ride the effect graph.

entries.title: Extended-effect declaration failure

entries.checks: The rule checks event declarations against the Model grammar and their declared consumers.

examples.after: # update the event declaration (or its consumers) to the current fields

fixOptions.description: Align the event declaration and its consumers on one declared payload shape.

entries.rationale: It matters because events are published facts; a malformed declaration would let producers and consumers disagree about what was published.
rootCauses: an event references payload fields that do not exist
a consumer subscribes to an event with an incompatible declared shape

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: published shapes are contracts.

targetNotes.note: Target transports project events per target policy; declarations are Model-level.

entries.title: Event declaration contract violation

entries.checks: The rule checks background-job declarations for admitted triggers, schedules and effect bindings.

examples.after: # declare the schedule in the job definition

fixOptions.description: Declare the trigger and align the job's effects with what it actually writes.

entries.rationale: It matters because jobs run without a caller present; undeclared or mis-declared jobs become unaccountable background behavior.
rootCauses: a job trigger references a schedule or event that is not declared
a job writes resources its declared effects do not cover

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: background behavior must be declared to be reviewable.

targetNotes.note: Per-target scheduling semantics are adapter concerns; the declaration is Model-level.

entries.title: Background job declaration violation

entries.checks: The rule records a call-like relationship that the declared graph cannot prove, keeping the edge visible as data instead of dropping it.

examples.after:
# explicit relation the graph can prove
triggers: handler_loader

fixOptions.description: Declare the relationship explicitly (command effect, scenario coverage or trace relation) so the edge becomes proven graph data.

entries.rationale: It matters because consumers who trust the declared graph as complete would miss real runtime calls; the diagnostic makes the gap explicit.
rootCauses: dynamic dispatch or reflection creates an edge the static grammar cannot express
a trace attachment claims a relation the Model does not declare

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: informational by design; the gap stays recorded even when accepted.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: the graph and its gaps are Model-level facts.

entries.title: Hidden call graph edge

entries.checks: The rule guards the content-addressed incremental cache: record shape, dependency keys and reuse eligibility.

examples.after:
lekalo cache clear --yes
lekalo load --project .   # recomputed
examples.before: lekalo load --project .   # uses possibly stale fragments

fixOptions.description: Clear the cache with the owned command (lekalo cache clear --yes) and re-run; the cache is derived data, never evidence.

entries.rationale: It matters because a cache that reuses more than its keys prove silently serves stale semantic results as fresh.
rootCauses: the cache was produced by a different product or contract version
a record's stored dependencies no longer match the current inputs
the SQLite store was modified outside the owned pipeline

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not applicable: clearing is always safe; the cache owns no unique data.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: cache records never encode target-specific state.

entries.title: Incremental cache record invalid

entries.checks: The rule guards what may be published: exported artifacts, their classification and their custody at the boundary.

examples.after: # classify, then export via the owning flow

fixOptions.description: Classify the artifact or publish through the owning flow so the boundary check sees reviewed bytes and declarations.

entries.rationale: It matters because publication is irreversible in practice; boundary checks are the last chance to keep unreviewed or classified material internal.
rootCauses: an artifact lacks the classification its destination requires
a published digest does not match the reviewed bytes

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: boundary decisions are explicit, not per-run.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral: publication rules ride the Model and authority matrix.

entries.title: Publication boundary violation

entries.checks: The rule enforces the authority matrix: which artifact kinds, homes and writers are admitted for each custody authority.

examples.after: node scripts/check-authority.mjs   # after regenerating through the owner

fixOptions.description: Remove the unauthorized artifact, re-produce it through the owning tool, and update the contract manifest with reviewed digests.

entries.rationale: It matters because the authority matrix is what stops tools from writing wherever they like; violations mean an unreviewed writer touched governed custody.
rootCauses: a tool wrote an artifact kind its authority never admitted
a contract manifest digest no longer matches the artifact bytes

severityProfile.waiverPolicy: Not waivable: authority boundaries are the integrity model.

targetNotes.note: Target-neutral.
